question: The Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Bill, 2024, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thu Aug 08 2024 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Bill, 2024, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **8th August 2024**.
 
• The bill aims to ensure fair representation of Scheduled Tribes in the assembly constituencies of Goa.
 
• It addresses the need for redrawing constituency boundaries based on updated demographic data.
 
• This legislation is part of a broader effort to enhance political inclusion and representation of marginalized communities.
 
• The introduction of the bill in the Lok Sabha marks the initial step in the legislative process for its enactment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**

 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are communities recognized by the Constitution of India as socially and economically disadvantaged.
 
• They are provided with specific measures for their protection and development under various legislative acts.
 
• Reservation in legislatures, government jobs, and educational institutions are part of these measures.
 
• The criteria for recognition as an ST include distinct culture, geographic isolation, and backwardness.
 
 
 
• **Delimitation**
 
 
• Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies based on the latest census data.
 
• This process ensures that each constituency has roughly equal population size for fair representation.
 
• In India, a Delimitation Commission is constituted to carry out this task.
 
• The last delimitation exercise was based on the 2001 Census, and a new one is expected based on the 2021 Census.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• The Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of 552 members.
 
• It is responsible for making laws and policies at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process in India**
 
 
• The legislative process involves the introduction of a bill in either house of Parliament.
 
• After introduction, the bill is debated and may be referred to a committee for further scrutiny.
 
• The bill must be passed by both houses of Parliament and receive the President's assent to become law.
 
• Important stages include the first reading, second reading, committee stage, and third reading.
